name: Afghanistan
fun_fact: The Bamiyan Buddhas stood for 1,500 years before being destroyed in 2001. They were taller than a 15 story building, carved directly into a cliff face.
hint: Land of the Hindu Kush mountains

name: Albania
fun_fact: Albania's communist dictator was so paranoid about invasion that he built 173,000 bunkers, roughly one for every 11 people. Most have never been used.

name: Algeria
fun_fact: Algeria is bigger than every country in Western Europe combined. The Sahara Desert alone covers 80% of its territory, an area larger than the entire Mediterranean Sea.

name: Andorra
fun_fact: Andorra has no airport, no railway, and no seaport. If you want to visit, you're driving through either France or Spain, there's literally no other way in.
hint: Tiny nation between France and Spain

name: Angola
fun_fact: Angola is one of the world's top diamond producers, but it's also where the giant sable antelope lives, a creature so rare it was thought to be extinct until 2004.

name: Antigua and Barbuda
fun_fact: Antigua and Barbuda has exactly 365 beaches on the main island, one for every day of the year. Locals actually joke about which one is for leap years.

name: Argentina
fun_fact: Buenos Aires has more bookstores per capita than any city on Earth. Argentina also invented the ballpoint pen, a Hungarian designed it, but an Argentine manufactured it first.

name: Armenia
fun_fact: Armenia was the first nation to adopt Christianity as a state religion in 301 AD. They also produce some of the oldest wine in the world, with a 6,100 year old winery found in a cave.

name: Australia
fun_fact: Australia is wider than the moon (by about 600 km). It's also the only continent country where you can drive for 14 hours and still be in the same state.
hint: Home of kangaroos and the Great Barrier Reef

name: Austria
fun_fact: Austria has produced more Nobel laureates per capita than almost any country. Mozart, Freud, Schrödinger, something in the Viennese coffee must help.

name: Azerbaijan
fun_fact: Azerbaijan is known as the Land of Fire because parts of the country literally burn continuously. Yanar Dag is a natural gas fire that has been blazing non stop for decades.

name: Bahamas
fun_fact: The Bahamas has the clearest water in the world, visibility can reach over 200 feet. It's also home to the famous swimming pigs of Exuma.

name: Bahrain
fun_fact: Bahrain is an island kingdom connected to Saudi Arabia by a 25 km bridge. It was the first place in the Middle East to discover oil in 1932.
hint: Island kingdom in the Persian Gulf

name: Bangladesh
fun_fact: Cox's Bazar in Bangladesh is 150 km of unbroken sandy beach, the longest natural sea beach on the planet. You could walk it for three straight days and never run out of shoreline.

name: Barbados
fun_fact: Barbados is the birthplace of rum. They've been commercially producing it since 1703, making Mount Gay the oldest existing rum brand in the world.

name: Belarus
fun_fact: Belarus is home to the Belovezhskaya Pushcha, Europe's last primeval forest. It's the only place where European bison still roam completely free.
hint: Home of Europe's last primeval forest

name: Belgium
fun_fact: Belgium produces over 220,000 tonnes of chocolate every year, but their real flex is having over 1,000 different varieties of beer.

name: Belize
fun_fact: Belize has the Great Blue Hole, a massive marine sinkhole that's visible from space. It's 300 meters across and incredibly deep, made famous by Jacques Cousteau.
hint: Home of the Great Blue Hole

name: Benin
fun_fact: Benin is the absolute birthplace of Voodoo (Vodun). It's an officially recognized religion there, celebrated with a massive festival every January.

name: Bhutan
fun_fact: Bhutan doesn't measure GDP. Instead, they track 'Gross National Happiness' and they're serious about it. The government surveys every citizen on their wellbeing.

name: Bolivia
fun_fact: Salar de Uyuni in Bolivia is so perfectly flat and reflective that when it rains, you literally can't tell where the sky ends and the ground begins. Satellites use it to calibrate their instruments.

name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
fun_fact: Sarajevo is one of the only cities in Europe where you can find a mosque, a Catholic church, an Orthodox church, and a synagogue all in the same neighborhood.

name: Botswana
fun_fact: Botswana is home to the Okavango Delta, a massive inland river system that doesn't flow into any ocean, it just evaporates into the Kalahari Desert.

name: Brazil
fun_fact: The Amazon produces 20% of the world's oxygen and is home to 10% of all species on Earth. One in ten known animals on the planet lives in Brazil's backyard.
hint: Home of Carnival and the Amazon

name: Brunei
fun_fact: The Sultan of Brunei lives in the world's largest residential palace. It has 1,788 rooms, 257 bathrooms, and a banquet hall that seats 5,000 people.

name: Bulgaria
fun_fact: Bulgaria produces 85% of the world's rose oil. The Valley of Roses is so productive that Bulgarian oil is a key ingredient in almost every luxury perfume.

name: Burkina Faso
fun_fact: Burkina Faso translates to 'Land of Honest Men'. It also hosts FESPACO, the largest African film festival, which transforms the capital every two years.

name: Burundi
fun_fact: Burundi has a traditional drumming culture so intense and unique that the Royal Drummers of Burundi are protected by UNESCO. The drums are carved from single tree trunks.

name: Cabo Verde
fun_fact: Cabo Verde was completely uninhabited until Portuguese explorers found it in 1456. Now it's a massive cultural melting pot famous for its Morna music.
hint: Atlantic island nation off West Africa

name: Cambodia
fun_fact: Angkor Wat in Cambodia is the largest religious monument in the world. It was originally built as a Hindu temple before transforming into a Buddhist site.

name: Cameroon
fun_fact: Cameroon is often called 'Africa in miniature' because it contains every single major climate and geographical zone found across the entire continent.

name: Canada
fun_fact: Canada's coastline is 202,080 km long. If you walked it non stop, it would take you over 30 years. It also has more lakes than every other country combined.
hint: Land of maple syrup and hockey

name: Central African Republic
fun_fact: The Central African Republic is one of the best places in the world to see forest elephants and western lowland gorillas, thanks to the pristine Dzanga Sangha reserve.

name: Chad
fun_fact: Lake Chad was once one of the largest freshwater lakes in the world, but it has shrunk by 95% since the 1960s, a dramatic shift visible from space.

name: Chile
fun_fact: Chile is so absurdly long and thin that if you tipped it on its side from Africa, it would stretch from Lisbon to Moscow. Some parts are narrower than Manhattan is long.
hint: World's longest country north to south

name: China
fun_fact: The Great Wall is longer than the distance from New York to Sydney. It took over 2,000 years to build, and contrary to the myth, you can't actually see it from space.

name: Colombia
fun_fact: Colombia produces 70 to 90% of the world's emeralds. The Spanish conquistadors went to absurd lengths to find their mines, the indigenous people kept them secret for generations.

name: Comoros
fun_fact: The Comoros islands are known as the 'Perfume Islands' because they are one of the world's leading producers of ylang ylang, the core scent in Chanel No. 5.
hint: Perfume islands of the Indian Ocean

name: Costa Rica
fun_fact: Costa Rica dissolved its entire military in 1948 and put the budget into education and healthcare. It's one of the happiest countries on Earth.

name: Cote d'Ivoire
fun_fact: Cote d'Ivoire is the undisputed king of chocolate, producing nearly 40% of the world's cocoa beans. The country is literally the engine of the global chocolate industry.

name: Croatia
fun_fact: The necktie was invented in Croatia. During the 17th century, Croatian mercenaries wore distinctive knotted neckcloths, which the French quickly copied and called 'cravates'.

name: Cuba
fun_fact: Cuba has a 99.8% literacy rate, higher than the US, UK, and France. They also have more doctors per capita than almost any country on Earth.
hint: Island of classic cars and cigars

name: Cyprus
fun_fact: According to Greek mythology, Cyprus is the birthplace of Aphrodite, the goddess of love. The island is totally split between Greek and Turkish communities today.

name: Czech Republic
fun_fact: The Czech Republic consumes more beer per capita than any other country in the world, and it's not even close. They invented the Pilsner style of beer in 1842.
hint: World's top beer consumers per capita

name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
fun_fact: The Congo River is the deepest river in the world, plunging over 220 meters deep in some spots. It's so powerful it could theoretically power all of sub Saharan Africa.
hint: Home of the world's deepest river

name: Denmark
fun_fact: The Danish flag has been in continuous use since 1219, over 800 years. Legend says it literally fell from the sky during a battle, and they've never put it down since.

name: Djibouti
fun_fact: Djibouti contains Lake Assal, which is the lowest point in Africa and ten times saltier than the ocean. It's so hot and salty that massive salt formations cover the shores.

name: Dominica
fun_fact: Dominica is called the 'Nature Isle' and is home to the Boiling Lake, the second largest hot spring in the world. The water actually boils from volcanic heat.

name: Dominican Republic
fun_fact: Santo Domingo in the Dominican Republic is the oldest continuously inhabited European settlement in the Americas, founded by Christopher Columbus's brother in 1496.
hint: Oldest European city in the Americas

name: Ecuador
fun_fact: Ecuador is named exactly after the equator. Because the Earth bulges at the middle, Mount Chimborazo in Ecuador is actually the closest point on Earth to space, not Everest.

name: Egypt
fun_fact: The Great Pyramid held the record for tallest human made structure for 3,800 years. Nothing surpassed it until Lincoln Cathedral in 1311. We still can't fully explain how it was built.
hint: Land of the Pharaohs and pyramids

name: El Salvador
fun_fact: El Salvador is the only country in Central America without a Caribbean coastline. It's totally Pacific, making it a legendary, albeit tiny, surfing destination.

name: Equatorial Guinea
fun_fact: Equatorial Guinea is the only country in Africa where Spanish is an official language. Despite being in Africa, its capital city is located on an island.

name: Eritrea
fun_fact: Asmara, the capital of Eritrea, is known as the 'Miami of Africa'. It's packed with impeccably preserved Italian Art Deco architecture from the 1930s.

name: Estonia
fun_fact: Estonia is so digitally advanced that you can vote, pay taxes, and sign legal documents online. They even declared internet access a basic human right in 2000.

name: Eswatini
fun_fact: Eswatini (formerly Swaziland) is one of the last absolute monarchies in the world. The King hosts the massive Umhlanga reed dance every year with tens of thousands of participants.

name: Ethiopia
fun_fact: A goat herder named Kaldi noticed his goats dancing after eating certain berries. That's the origin story of coffee, and it happened in Ethiopia around the 9th century.

name: Fiji
fun_fact: Fiji is made of exactly 333 islands. They also have a unique tradition called sevusevu, where visitors must present a bundle of kava root to the village chief upon arriving.

name: Finland
fun_fact: Finland has 3.3 million saunas for 5.5 million people, that's roughly one sauna for every two Finns. Important business meetings happen in saunas.

name: France
fun_fact: France gets more tourists per year than it has citizens, roughly 90 million visitors for a population of 67 million. Paris alone gets more visitors than any other city.

name: Gabon
fun_fact: Over 80% of Gabon is covered by pristine rainforest. They're doing such a good job conserving it that they are actually paid by the UN to keep their forests intact.

name: Gambia
fun_fact: The Gambia is the smallest country in mainland Africa, and it's basically just a sliver of land bordering the Gambia River, completely surrounded by Senegal.

name: Georgia
fun_fact: Georgia has been making wine for 8,000 years, making it the oldest wine producing region on Earth. They still make it the ancient way, buried underground in clay jars called qvevri.

name: Germany
fun_fact: Germany has over 1,500 types of beer, but they also have over 3,000 varieties of bread. Germans take their bread so seriously that their bread culture is a UNESCO heritage.

name: Ghana
fun_fact: Ghana was the very first sub Saharan African nation to declare independence from European colonization in 1957. It paved the way for the rest of the continent.
hint: First sub-Saharan nation to gain independence

name: Greece
fun_fact: Greece has more archaeological museums than any other country, but here's what hits harder: democracy, the Olympics, Western philosophy, and theater were all invented in Athens.

name: Grenada
fun_fact: Grenada is known as the 'Spice Isle' because this tiny island produces over 20% of the world's nutmeg, a massive chunk of the global supply.
hint: The Spice Isle of the Caribbean

name: Guatemala
fun_fact: Guatemala is the true birthplace of chocolate. The ancient Maya civilization were the first to roast cacao beans and create a bitter, spicy chocolate drink thousands of years ago.

name: Guinea
fun_fact: Guinea has a massive chunk of the world's bauxite reserves, the raw material used to make aluminum. Despite this wealth, much of the country remains incredibly wild.

name: Guinea-Bissau
fun_fact: Guinea Bissau is composed of an archipelago of 88 islands where matriarchal societies still exist. On some islands, women hold all the economic and social power.

name: Guyana
fun_fact: Guyana is the only country in South America where English is the official language. A massive 80% of the country is untouched tropical rainforest.

name: Haiti
fun_fact: Haiti was the very first free black republic in the world. They successfully overthrew their colonizers in a massive slave revolt and declared independence in 1804.

name: Honduras
fun_fact: Honduras is home to Copan, an ancient Mayan city that has the most detailed and intricate stone carvings of any Mayan site in existence.
hint: Home of ancient Mayan ruins at Copan

name: Hungary
fun_fact: The Rubik's Cube was invented by a Hungarian architect, Erno Rubik, in 1974. He originally built it just to help his students understand 3D geometry.

name: Iceland
fun_fact: Iceland is one of the very few inhabited places on Earth with zero mosquitoes. Scientists still aren't 100% sure why, but it involves their unique freeze thaw cycles.
hint: Land of fire and ice with no mosquitoes

name: India
fun_fact: India's postal service delivers to over 1.5 billion people and has a floating post office on Dal Lake in Kashmir. It's the largest postal network on the planet.

name: Indonesia
fun_fact: Indonesia is a massive archipelago of over 17,000 islands. It's home to the Komodo dragon, the heaviest lizard on Earth, which has venomous saliva.

name: Iran
fun_fact: Iran, formerly Persia, is home to one of the world's oldest continuous major civilizations. They've been weaving the world's most intricate carpets for over 2,500 years.

name: Iraq
fun_fact: Iraq is the cradle of civilization. Ancient Mesopotamia, located here, is where humanity invented writing (cuneiform), the wheel, and the 60 minute hour.
hint: Cradle of civilization â€” ancient Mesopotamia

name: Ireland
fun_fact: Ireland's famous Guinness brewery in Dublin was leased by its founder in 1759 for 9,000 years at an annual rent of just 45 pounds. They're locked in for a while.

name: Israel
fun_fact: Israel has the highest number of tech startups per capita in the world. The technology behind USB flash drives and Waze GPS was invented here.
hint: Startup nation of the Middle East

name: Italy
fun_fact: Italy has more UNESCO World Heritage sites than any other country in the world. They also have a free, 24 hour public wine fountain in the Abruzzo region.
hint: Home of pizza, pasta, and the Colosseum

name: Jamaica
fun_fact: Jamaica produces some of the fastest runners in human history. It's also the birthplace of reggae, and James Bond was entirely created by Ian Fleming at his Jamaican estate.
hint: Birthplace of reggae and Bob Marley

name: Japan
fun_fact: Kongō Gumi, founded in 578 AD, operated continuously for 1,400 years building Buddhist temples. Japan has thousands of businesses over 200 years old.
hint: Home of sumo, sushi, and cherry blossoms

name: Jordan
fun_fact: Petra in Jordan is an entire ancient city carved directly into vibrant red sandstone cliff faces. It was lost to the Western world for centuries until discovered in 1812.
hint: Home of the ancient city of Petra

name: Kazakhstan
fun_fact: Kazakhstan is the world's largest landlocked country. It's so massive that it's larger than all of Western Europe combined, yet has a population smaller than New York State.

name: Kenya
fun_fact: Kenya is the world's original safari destination. It's also home to the Great Rift Valley, a massive geological trench that is literally splitting the African continent apart.

name: Kiribati
fun_fact: Kiribati is the only country in the world situated in all four hemispheres (North, South, East, and West). Sadly, it's heavily threatened by rising sea levels.
hint: Only country in all four hemispheres

name: Kosovo
fun_fact: Kosovo is the youngest country in Europe, declaring independence in 2008. Over 70% of its population is under 35, making it the youngest population in Europe too.
hint: Europe's youngest nation, declared independence in 2008

name: Kuwait
fun_fact: The Kuwaiti Dinar is the highest valued currency in the world. One Dinar is usually worth more than three US Dollars, thanks to massive oil reserves.

name: Kyrgyzstan
fun_fact: Kyrgyzstan is almost entirely mountainous, often called the 'Switzerland of Central Asia'. It has one of the world's largest natural walnut forests.

name: Laos
fun_fact: Laos is the most heavily bombed country per capita in history. Millions of unexploded bombs from the Vietnam War era still litter the countryside today.

name: Latvia
fun_fact: Latvia has an incredibly fast internet speed, often ranking in the top 10 globally. Over half the country is covered in thick, pristine forests.
hint: Baltic state with Art Nouveau capital

name: Lebanon
fun_fact: Lebanon is home to Byblos, one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, dating back over 7,000 years. The word 'Bible' actually comes from Byblos.
hint: Home of the oldest city, Byblos

name: Lesotho
fun_fact: Lesotho is entirely surrounded by South Africa and is the only country in the world that lies entirely above 1,000 meters in elevation. It's the 'Kingdom in the Sky'.

name: Liberia
fun_fact: Liberia was founded in the 1820s by freed American slaves. Its flag closely resembles the US flag, and its capital, Monrovia, is named after US President James Monroe.

name: Libya
fun_fact: Libya is more than 90% desert. However, buried deep under the Sahara is the Nubian Sandstone Aquifer System, the world's largest known fossil water aquifer.
hint: North African nation that is 90% desert

name: Liechtenstein
fun_fact: Liechtenstein is so small it doesn't have an airport or a military. It's also the world's largest exporter of false teeth, producing over 60 million a year.
hint: Tiny Alpine country between Switzerland and Austria

name: Lithuania
fun_fact: Lithuania was the very last country in Europe to adopt Christianity. They held onto their pagan roots and nature worship until the late 14th century.

name: Luxembourg
fun_fact: Luxembourg is incredibly wealthy, boasting the highest GDP per capita in the world. In 2020, it became the first country to make all public transport entirely free.
hint: Tiny but richest country per capita

name: Madagascar
fun_fact: Because Madagascar has been isolated for millions of years, about 90% of its plants and animals, like all species of lemurs, are found literally nowhere else on Earth.
hint: Island of lemurs and unique wildlife

name: Malawi
fun_fact: Lake Malawi contains more species of fish than any other lake in the world, over 1,000 distinct species of vibrant cichlids that are popular in home aquariums.

name: Malaysia
fun_fact: Malaysia's Petronas Twin Towers were the tallest buildings in the world until 2004. The country also has the world's largest underground cave chamber, the Sarawak Chamber.
hint: Home of the Petronas Twin Towers

name: Maldives
fun_fact: The Maldives is the lowest lying country on Earth, with an average ground level of just 1.5 meters above sea level. They held a famous underwater cabinet meeting to protest climate change.

name: Mali
fun_fact: Timbuktu in Mali was once one of the wealthiest and most important centers of learning in the world. It was a legendary trading hub for gold, salt, and books.

name: Malta
fun_fact: Malta has some of the oldest free standing stone structures in the world. The Megalithic Temples of Malta are older than Stonehenge and the Pyramids of Giza.

name: Marshall Islands
fun_fact: The Marshall Islands were used by the US for 67 nuclear tests in the mid 20th century. Today, it's home to the largest shark sanctuary in the world.
hint: Pacific atoll nation and nuclear test site

name: Mauritania
fun_fact: Mauritania is home to the 'Eye of the Sahara', a massive, deeply eroded geological dome that looks exactly like a giant bullseye from space.
hint: Home of the Eye of the Sahara

name: Mauritius
fun_fact: Mauritius was the only known habitat of the dodo bird, which went extinct in the 1600s. Today, it's one of Africa's most prosperous and democratic nations.
hint: Where the dodo bird once lived

name: Mexico
fun_fact: Mexico City is built over a drained lake and is literally sinking at a rate of up to 20 inches per year. It's also the oldest capital city in the Americas.
hint: Land of tacos, temples, and tequila

name: Micronesia
fun_fact: Micronesia is made up of 607 islands. It's home to Nan Madol, an ancient ruined city built on artificial islands connected by canals, often called the 'Venice of the Pacific'.

name: Moldova
fun_fact: Moldova has the largest wine cellar in the world. The Mileștii Mici cellar stretches for 200 kilometers underground and holds nearly 2 million bottles of wine.

name: Monaco
fun_fact: Monaco is smaller than New York's Central Park. It's so densely populated with millionaires that roughly one in three residents is classified as a millionaire.
hint: Playground of the rich on the French Riviera

name: Mongolia
fun_fact: Mongolia is the most sparsely populated country in the world. It's a vast landscape where traditional nomadic culture, living in gers (yurts), is still very much alive.
hint: Land of Genghis Khan and endless steppes

name: Montenegro
fun_fact: Montenegro literally translates to 'Black Mountain'. It features the Tara River Canyon, the deepest canyon in Europe, plunging over 1,300 meters deep.
hint: The Black Mountain of the Balkans

name: Morocco
fun_fact: Morocco was the very first country to formally recognize the newly independent United States in 1777. The Moroccan American Treaty of Friendship is the US's oldest unbroken treaty.

name: Mozambique
fun_fact: Mozambique is the only national flag in the world that features a modern assault rifle. The AK 47 on the flag symbolizes defense and vigilance.
hint: Only flag in the world with an AK-47

name: Myanmar
fun_fact: Myanmar is home to Bagan, an ancient city that contains over 10,000 incredibly preserved Buddhist temples and pagodas stretching across a massive plain.

name: Namibia
fun_fact: Namibia has the oldest desert in the world, the Namib. It's also the first country in Africa to explicitly include environmental protection in its national constitution.
hint: Home of the world's oldest desert

name: Nauru
fun_fact: Nauru is the smallest island nation in the world at just 21 square kilometers. It was once incredibly wealthy from phosphate mining, but the resources were totally depleted.

name: Nepal
fun_fact: Nepal is the only country whose flag isn't rectangular, it's two stacked triangles. The exact mathematical proportions are even defined directly in their constitution.
hint: The only country with a non-rectangular flag

name: Netherlands
fun_fact: About one third of the Netherlands lies entirely below sea level. They are masters of water management, holding back the ocean with massive networks of dikes and pumps.

name: New Zealand
fun_fact: New Zealand gave women the right to vote in 1893, a full 27 years before the US and 35 years before the UK. The petition that made it happen was the longest signed document in the country's history.

name: Nicaragua
fun_fact: Nicaragua has the only freshwater lake in the world containing oceanic animal life, including freshwater sharks, swordfish, and tarpon that adapted to the lake.

name: Niger
fun_fact: Niger is home to some of the largest and most pristine dinosaur fossil beds in the world, buried deep within the sands of the Sahara desert.
hint: Saharan nation with ancient dinosaur fossils

name: Nigeria
fun_fact: Nigeria's film industry, Nollywood, produces over 2,500 movies a year. That makes it the second largest film industry in the world by volume, ahead of Hollywood.

name: North Korea
fun_fact: North Korea uses its own calendar, the Juche calendar, which begins counting from the birth year of its founder, Kim Il sung (1912).

name: North Macedonia
fun_fact: Mother Teresa was born in Skopje, the capital of North Macedonia, in 1910. The country is also famous for its incredibly pristine Ohrid pearls.

name: Norway
fun_fact: Raw salmon wasn't traditional Japanese sushi, Norway literally convinced Japan to try it in the 1980s as a marketing strategy. Now it's the most popular sushi globally.
hint: Land of fjords and the Northern Lights

name: Oman
fun_fact: Oman is the oldest continuously independent state in the Arab world. It's famous for producing frankincense, resin extracted from desert trees, prized since antiquity.

name: Pakistan
fun_fact: Pakistan has the second highest mountain on Earth, K2, and also contains the Khewra Salt Mine, the second largest salt mine in the world where pink Himalayan salt is harvested.
hint: Home of K2 and the Indus Valley

name: Palau
fun_fact: Palau was the first country in the world to officially ban all shark fishing, creating a massive marine sanctuary the size of France to protect them.
hint: First country to ban shark fishing

name: Panama
fun_fact: Panama is the only place in the world where you can see the sun rise on the Pacific Ocean and set on the Atlantic Ocean, due to the curve of the isthmus.
hint: Where two oceans meet through a canal

name: Papua New Guinea
fun_fact: Papua New Guinea is the most linguistically diverse country on Earth. With over 800 distinct languages spoken, it accounts for about 12% of the world's total languages.
hint: Most linguistically diverse country on Earth

name: Paraguay
fun_fact: Paraguay's flag is completely unique: it's the only national flag in the world that has different emblems on the front and the back.
hint: Only flag different on each side

name: Peru
fun_fact: Machu Picchu in Peru was built by the Inca in the 15th century but was completely unknown to the outside world until a local guide showed it to an American explorer in 1911.

name: Philippines
fun_fact: The Philippines is a massive archipelago made up of over 7,600 individual islands. It's also the undisputed text messaging capital of the world.

name: Poland
fun_fact: Poland has the world's largest castle by land area, Malbork Castle, built entirely of brick by the Teutonic Knights in the 13th century.
hint: Home of Copernicus and The Witcher

name: Portugal
fun_fact: Portugal is the oldest nation state in Europe, keeping the exact same defined borders since the year 1139. It's also the world's largest producer of cork.
hint: Europe's oldest country with unchanged borders

name: Qatar
fun_fact: Qatar is so arid that it has no natural rivers or lakes at all. Almost all of its fresh water is produced through massive, energy intensive desalination plants.

name: Republic of the Congo
fun_fact: Brazzaville in the Republic of the Congo and Kinshasa in the DRC are the closest two capital cities in the world, sitting right across the Congo River from each other.

name: Romania
fun_fact: The Palace of the Parliament in Romania is the heaviest building on Earth, constructed from 1.5 billion pounds of steel and bronze, and massive amounts of marble.

name: Russia
fun_fact: Russia is so unimaginably massive that it spans 11 different time zones. You could be eating breakfast in Moscow while someone in Vladivostok is having dinner.
hint: Largest country in the world spanning 11 time zones

name: Rwanda
fun_fact: Rwanda has the highest percentage of women in parliament of any country in the world, holding over 60% of the seats. It's also famous for mountain gorilla conservation.

name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
fun_fact: Saint Kitts and Nevis is the smallest sovereign state in the Western Hemisphere, both in land area and population. It was the first English colony in the Caribbean.

name: Saint Lucia
fun_fact: Saint Lucia is the only country in the world named entirely after a historical woman, Saint Lucy of Syracuse. It's famous for the Pitons, two massive volcanic spires.
hint: The only country named after a woman

name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
fun_fact: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines was a major filming location for the 'Pirates of the Caribbean' movies, thanks to its stunning and relatively untouched shorelines.
hint: Where Pirates of the Caribbean was filmed

name: Samoa
fun_fact: Samoa completely skipped Friday, December 30, 2011. They jumped straight to Saturday to align their time zone with their main trading partners, Australia and New Zealand.

name: San Marino
fun_fact: San Marino is the oldest surviving republic in the world, founded by a stonemason in the year 301 AD. It's entirely surrounded by Italy.

name: Sao Tome and Principe
fun_fact: Sao Tome and Principe is the smallest African country. It's so perfectly positioned that it's the closest country on Earth to the intersection of the Equator and the Prime Meridian.

name: Saudi Arabia
fun_fact: Saudi Arabia is the largest country in the world entirely without a single permanent river. The country relies heavily on wadis (seasonal riverbeds) and desalination.

name: Senegal
fun_fact: Senegal is home to Lake Retba, which is naturally a vivid, bright pink color due to a specific type of salt loving algae that thrives in its hyper saline waters.
hint: Western tip of Africa, end of the Dakar Rally

name: Serbia
fun_fact: Nikola Tesla, one of the greatest inventors in history, was an ethnic Serb. Today, the Serbian capital of Belgrade houses the Nikola Tesla Museum holding all his original patents.

name: Seychelles
fun_fact: The Seychelles contains the Aldabra Atoll, home to over 150,000 giant tortoises. There are vastly more giant tortoises in the Seychelles than people.
hint: Indian Ocean paradise with giant tortoises

name: Sierra Leone
fun_fact: Sierra Leone's capital, Freetown, was literally founded as a home for freed slaves from London and the Americas in the late 18th century.

name: Singapore
fun_fact: Singapore is one of only three true city states left in the world (along with Monaco and Vatican City). It also boasts the world's tallest indoor waterfall.

name: Slovakia
fun_fact: Slovakia has the highest number of castles and chateaux per capita in the world. There are over 100 castles and 400 manor houses scattered across the small country.
hint: Most castles per capita in the world

name: Slovenia
fun_fact: Slovenia is incredibly green, over 60% of the country is covered in dense forest. It's also the only country in the world with the word 'LOVE' right in its name.
hint: Alpine gem with LOVE in its name

name: Solomon Islands
fun_fact: The Solomon Islands are a hotspot for WWII history, with dozens of sunken warships and planes resting in the shallow, incredibly biodiverse coral reefs.

name: Somalia
fun_fact: Somalia has the longest coastline in mainland Africa. Due to its shape pointing into the Indian Ocean, it forms the tip of the region known as the Horn of Africa.
hint: Horn of Africa with the longest coastline

name: South Africa
fun_fact: South Africa is the only country in the world to voluntarily completely dismantle its own nuclear weapons program. It also has three distinct capital cities.

name: South Korea
fun_fact: South Korea has the fastest average internet speeds in the world, and competitive video gaming (esports) is treated as a major, highly respected national sport.

name: South Sudan
fun_fact: South Sudan is the absolute newest country on Earth. It officially gained its independence from Sudan in 2011 after decades of conflict.

name: Spain
fun_fact: Spain has a festival called La Tomatina where tens of thousands of people gather just to throw over 100 metric tons of overripe tomatoes at each other in the streets.
hint: Land of flamenco and La Sagrada Familia

name: Sri Lanka
fun_fact: Sri Lanka was formally known as Ceylon, which is why Ceylon Tea is still the country's most famous export. It's shaped like a teardrop falling from India.

name: Sudan
fun_fact: Sudan actually has more ancient pyramids than Egypt. There are over 200 steep Nubian pyramids scattered across the desert, built by the ancient Kingdom of Kush.

name: Suriname
fun_fact: Suriname is the smallest country in South America, and one of the greenest on Earth. A staggering 93% of the country is covered in pristine Amazonian rainforest.

name: Sweden
fun_fact: Sweden is heavily forested, but it also has over 267,000 islands, making it the country with the most islands in the world. Only about 1,000 of them are inhabited.
hint: Home of IKEA, Spotify, and ABBA

name: Switzerland
fun_fact: Switzerland hasn't been in a state of war since 1815. They take neutrality so seriously that their mountains are hollowed out with military bunkers and artillery.
hint: Neutral nation of chocolate and watches

name: Syria
fun_fact: Damascus, the capital of Syria, is widely considered the oldest continuously inhabited city in the world, with evidence of civilization stretching back 11,000 years.

name: Taiwan
fun_fact: Taiwan produces over 90% of the world's most advanced semiconductors. If you're using a modern smartphone or laptop, a chip from Taiwan is almost certainly powering it.
hint: Silicon island powering the world's tech

name: Tajikistan
fun_fact: Tajikistan is known as the 'Roof of the World' because over 90% of its landmass is incredibly high, rugged mountains. It's a paradise for extreme alpinists.
hint: Roof of the World â€” over 93% mountains

name: Tanzania
fun_fact: Tanzania is home to Mount Kilimanjaro, the highest free standing mountain in the world, meaning it's not part of a mountain range, it just rises massively from the plains.
hint: Home of Kilimanjaro and the Serengeti

name: Thailand
fun_fact: Thailand is the only Southeast Asian country that was never colonized by a European power. The name literally translates to 'Land of the Free'.

name: Timor-Leste
fun_fact: Timor Leste (East Timor) is one of the world's newest countries, gaining independence in 2002. It's one of only two predominantly Catholic countries in Asia.

name: Togo
fun_fact: Togo is incredibly narrow, stretching just 115 km wide in some places, but stretching deep into Africa. It has a massive Voodoo market in its capital, Lome.

name: Tonga
fun_fact: Tonga is the only monarchy in the Pacific that was never completely colonized. It's also one of the few places on Earth you can swim with migrating humpback whales.
hint: Pacific kingdom that was never colonized

name: Trinidad and Tobago
fun_fact: Trinidad and Tobago is the absolute birthplace of the steel drum (steelpan), the only major acoustic instrument invented in the 20th century, made from oil barrels.

name: Tunisia
fun_fact: Tunisia contains the ancient ruins of Carthage, the legendary city that once rivaled Rome. It's also heavily featured as the planet Tatooine in the Star Wars films.

name: Turkey
fun_fact: Istanbul, Turkey, is the only major city in the world that straddles two distinct continents, Europe and Asia, physically separated by the Bosphorus Strait.
hint: Where East meets West across the Bosphorus

name: Turkmenistan
fun_fact: Turkmenistan is home to the 'Door to Hell', a massive natural gas crater that has been continuously burning in the middle of the Karakum Desert since 1971.
hint: Home of the burning Door to Hell

name: Tuvalu
fun_fact: Tuvalu is so small and remote that it earns a massive chunk of its national income just from leasing out its highly desirable internet domain extension: .tv.
hint: Nation that profits from the .tv domain

name: Uganda
fun_fact: Uganda is incredibly biodiverse and is one of the only places on Earth where you can trek to see endangered mountain gorillas in their natural cloud forest habitat.
hint: Pearl of Africa with mountain gorillas

name: Ukraine
fun_fact: Ukraine has the deepest metro station in the world, Arsenalna in Kyiv. It's so deep (105.5 meters) that taking the escalator down takes a full five minutes.

name: United Arab Emirates
fun_fact: The UAE transformed Dubai from a small desert port into a futuristic megacity in just 30 years. It's home to the Burj Khalifa, the tallest structure ever built by humans.
hint: Home of the world's tallest building

name: United Kingdom
fun_fact: The United Kingdom has arguably shaped the modern world more than any other nation, inventing the steam engine, the World Wide Web, and modern football.
hint: Island nation that invented the world wide web

name: United States
fun_fact: The United States has no official language at the federal level. It also contains every single climate zone on Earth, from arctic tundra to tropical rainforest.
hint: Land of the free with 50 states

name: Uruguay
fun_fact: Uruguay was the very first country in the world to completely legalize the recreational use of marijuana nationwide in 2013. It also runs on 98% renewable energy.

name: Uzbekistan
fun_fact: Uzbekistan is one of only two 'doubly landlocked' countries in the world, meaning to reach an ocean, you have to cross at least two other countries' borders.

name: Vanuatu
fun_fact: Bungee jumping originated in Vanuatu. Local men perform a ritual called land diving, leaping from massive wooden towers with only vines tied to their ankles.

name: Vatican City
fun_fact: Vatican City is the world's smallest country at just 0.44 sq km, smaller than most city parks. Yet it has its own post office, radio station, and an ATM with Latin instructions.
hint: World's smallest country, home to the Pope

name: Venezuela
fun_fact: Venezuela is home to Angel Falls, the world's highest uninterrupted waterfall. The water drops a massive 979 meters, so far that much of it turns to mist before hitting the ground.
hint: Home of Angel Falls, the world's highest waterfall

name: Vietnam
fun_fact: Vietnam is the world's second largest exporter of coffee, right behind Brazil. They popularized robusta beans and serve it strong with sweetened condensed milk.

name: Yemen
fun_fact: Yemen is home to Shibam, an ancient city known as the 'Manhattan of the Desert'. It's packed with 500 year old mudbrick skyscrapers towering up to 11 stories high.
hint: Home of the alien-looking Socotra Island

name: Zambia
fun_fact: Zambia shares the magnificent Victoria Falls with Zimbabwe. It's also home to the massive Kasanka bat migration, where 10 million fruit bats darken the sky.
hint: Home to Victoria Falls, the smoke that thunders

name: Zimbabwe
fun_fact: Zimbabwe has one of the world's highest literacy rates in Africa at over 90%. It also went through hyperinflation so extreme they printed a 100 Trillion dollar note.
hint: Land of the 100 trillion dollar bill
